short.en: Click a cell, wire it in

t.en: From this chapter on, the computing is done by a little robot. It walks through the whole table cell by cell and does the same thing on every cell.
This level has a single row of cells, and the leftmost one already holds a number. The robot starts on cell 2 and walks right, and on each cell it copies the number from the cell to its left.

How does the robot know to copy from the left? From the circuit board you wire up. The inputs pane shows the robot’s view: the red frame in the middle is the cell it stands on, where the result is written. The View part on the left of the circuit board is that view: click the “left” cell, and the part gains an output that brings that cell’s number into the circuit.

Finally, drag a wire from the dot under the “left” input to “this cell”, the red-framed output at the bottom of the board. It means: whatever comes from the left, write it in this cell. You can also click one dot and then the other.

goal.en: Have the robot copy the number in the leftmost cell, cell by cell, all the way to the right: every cell equals the cell to its left.

how.en: Click the “left” cell in the view: the View part gets an output for it. Wire that to “this cell”, then click “Run tests”.

body.en: You drew a single wire, and the robot carried it out on every cell. The circuit board is the rule: you write it once, and the robot uses it on every cell.

note.en: A circuit board describes the rule for one cell; the robot runs it on every cell.

say.en: Step 1: click the “left” cell in the view, and the “View” part gains an output.
Step 2: drag a wire from the dot on the “View” part’s right to “this cell”.
Step 3: click “Run tests” and watch the robot copy its way along, cell by cell.
The robot walks from left to right, so when it reaches a cell, the cell to its right is still empty and can’t be read.

hints.en: Click “left” in the view, then wire the new output on the “View” part to “this cell”.
